children: There's now a shortage of oil supertankers, adding more pressure on gasoline prices, with shipping rates reaching record levels around the world.
Attacks on Saudi Arabia's bypass pipeline earlier this month forced more crude back through the Strait of Hormuz,
The Wall Street Journal
reported, further straining a tanker fleet that's already stretched thin.
The tanker shortage is slowing oil deliveries just as record shipping costs squeeze refiners' margins, which could keep fuel prices high even if crude prices fall.
According to maritime intelligence firm Windward, the cost of hiring an oil supertanker to load inside the Persian Gulf and transit the Strait of Hormuz crossed $1M a day earlier this month.
That's $26 a barrel, or about a quarter of the crude's value based on current market prices. Shipping costs are generally only a fraction of a crude cargo's value,
WSJ
reported.
Average daily earnings for an oil supertanker reached $651,107 last Thursday, according to Clarksons Research, nearly double that of the prior week before Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline was shut.
The pipeline may be partially restarted within days, people familiar with Saudi Aramco's (
) operations told
WSJ
, but hurdles remain over some technical issues.

The port of Yanbu, Saudi Arabia's Red Sea export terminal, hasn't loaded any crude tankers since the attacks. Saudi-flagged vessels stopped transiting the Bab al-Mandeb Strait, which is now under Houthi control.

More than a dozen Saudi-flagged vessels have rerouted via the Cape of Good Hope in South Africa, at an extra cost of $1M a trip per vessel, Windward said. The detour also adds around two weeks to the journey, taking more supertankers off the market.
As a result, Aramco (

) is pushing more crude through the Strait of Hormuz using ship-to-ship transfers. This involves moving oil from Gulf terminals to ports just outside Hormuz, where it can be transferred to vessels headed to global markets.
While ship-to-ship transfers keep oil moving, they hold up vessels that would otherwise be available for other cargoes.

title: Oil supertanker shortage: Another risk for gas prices
